Low-Mileage Single-Owner 2008 Dodge Viper SRT-10 Roadster Dresses in Snakeskin Green Pearlcoat
88 photos
Photo: Motorcar Classics
Farmingdale, New York-based Motorcar Classics probably thinks it has you covered if you're willing to write a rather fat check for this cool ride – and just by looking at the snake, one can already feel bitten by a sudden urge to make its 8.4-liter V10 roar like there’s no tomorrow…
No, we don’t need a dose of antivenom – not if we’re bitten by something like this, because we’ll embrace its insanity with open minds and hearts. Anyway, the story of the Dodge Viper began as a crazy bet that no one except Bob Lutz thought it could be won. Back then, Chrysler’s president of operations had an idea in 1988: what if their company produced a true American sports car, but following the guidelines of the original Shelby Cobra?
Basically, Lutz thought it was a good idea to make a Chrysler model with crazy looks, raw and unabated power, plus great performance. Of course, as it turned out, the result was even more than the corner office head honcho had dreamt, although we have to say that his daringness to take a V10 engine that was being developed for the heavy-duty Dodge Ram pickup truck series and fit it into a sports car was pretty bonkers by any standards.
They also used suspension parts from the smaller Dakota model – which was also a pickup truck. We know, we know, it sounds like they were high on something, but it wasn’t just Lutz, as lead truck engineer François Castaing and Chrysler designer Tom Gale also fell in love with the project. Insanity was a common trait, it seems, as these were the roaring 1980s. Carroll Shelby himself later went with the Cobra-inspired Chrysler to the company’s CEO Lee Iacocca in support of his fellow comrades.
Photo: Motorcar Classics Upon approval, the concept was quickly brought to life – probably out of fear of the big kahunas sobering up and sending their ideas to the junk station. A concept car was ready within months, and the Viper was even brought to life on a very ‘small’ budget for an automaker like Chrysler, around $80 million. Naturally, with its looks and the sum of its parts, it was a flawed car, but the striking premise caused a massive sensation, and the Viper became a legend.
It was also a big contrast between the brawny looks and the number of people that were able to tame it, so early in the production years it was considered a massively intimidating car to drive, as there was massive power and torque but limited driver assistance from electronic nannies. That’s something almost inconceivable now, right?
Anyway, its legend only grew through the years, and Chrysler plus its later installments kept the Dodge Viper until 2017 and across five generations with a single small hiatus for the final installment. The fourth generation – ZB II – came out in 2008 and brought with it a new 8.4-liter V10 packing 600 horsepower and a massive 560 lb-ft of torque (759 Nm). This 2008 Dodge Viper SRT-10 Roadster is, of course, of the ZB II variety, and Farmingdale, New York-based Motorcar Classics “is proud to present this exceptional specimen of raw American muscle.”
Photo: Motorcar Classics This 2008 Dodge Viper SRT-10 has just 5,548 original miles, as it was in the care of a single owner all this time, and a clean CARFAX report, along with “an ideal history emerging from a prominent private collection.” Besides the fact that a design like the Viper won’t ever go unnoticed, the car is also dressed in a neck-snapping Viper Snakeskin Green Pearlcoat paint with white racing stripes and a black soft top, along with a classic black leather interior.
Of course, the dealership knows “this fourth-generation (ZB II) Viper represents a high point in American performance engineering, powered by a massive, naturally aspirated 8.4-liter V10 engine co-developed with McLaren Performance Technologies.” Its 600 hp and 560 lb-ft of torque channeled through a precise Tremec TR-6060 six-speed manual transmission are still worthy of our attention even today in the age of boring or plain ugly-looking EV hypercars boasting over 1,000 horsepower but also no soul whatsoever.
Photo: Motorcar Classics A representative of an age long gone, the “analogue beast rockets from 0 to 60 mph in under 3.5 seconds and commands a top speed exceeding 200 mph,” continues the description. They continue: “Beyond its overwhelming performance, this 2008 Viper holds immense historical and collectability significance. It stands as the quintessential expression of the traditional driver's supercar—offering pure, unadulterated mechanical engagement without electronic traction controls or driver aids to dilute the experience.”
The color is also sublime, and the ultra-low-mileage survivor is seen more like an “investment-grade opportunity for the discerning enthusiast or serious collector” than a thrill car for a true enthusiast. Of course, maybe it’s also the price that gets in the way, as the company asks $124,900 but leaves the door open for negotiations via the ‘make an offer’ button on their online listing. Cool or not?
